This three-foot warhorn, a revered artifact of Dhakaan, is carved from the tip of a red dragon's horn, banded with adamantine, and covered with runes of power. An inscription in Goblin reads "A mighty dirge for the fallen foe." Ghaal'duur was crafted by Jhazaal Dhakaan, a legendary dirge singer who united the ancient warring clans. Any kech warlord who obtained it would gain great influence among the Heirs of Dhakaan—and any non-Dhakaani that possesses it bears a dangerous burden.

description.name: Random Properties
description.value: The warhorn has the following random properties (see "Artifacts" in the Dungeon Master's Guide):

entries: 2 [minor beneficial](https://5e.tools/tables.html#artifact%20properties%3B%20minor%20beneficial%20properties_xdmg) properties

1 [minor detrimental](https://5e.tools/tables.html#artifact%20properties%3B%20minor%20detrimental%20properties_xdmg) property; any goblinoid attuned to the warhorn is immune to the detrimental effects of this property.

description.name: Jhazaal's Presence
description.value: While you are attuned to the warhorn, your Charisma increases by 4, to a maximum of 24.

description.name: The Dragon's Song
description.value: When holding the warhorn in both hands, you can use it as a Spellcasting Focus for your Bard spells. Bard spells cast using the warhorn gain the following benefits:

entries: If the spell has a duration of 1 minute or longer, its duration is doubled, to a maximum duration of 24 hours.
If the spell has a range of 5 feet or greater, its range is doubled.
If the spell is 1st level or higher, it is cast as if from a spell slot 1 level higher than the spell slot you expended.

description.name: The Sound of Victory
description.value: While holding the warhorn in both hands, you can take a Magic action to blow it, empowering your allies and intimidating your foes. For the next 10 minutes, any time an ally within 600 feet of you that can hear you makes an attack roll or a saving throw, it adds 1d4 to the attack roll or save. If the creature is a goblinoid, it adds 2d4 instead of 1d4. Additionally, every enemy within 600 feet of you that can hear you must make a Charisma saving throw against your Bard spell save DC. For the next 10 minutes, whenever a target that fails this save makes an attack roll or a saving throw before the spell ends, the target must subtract 1d4 from the attack roll or save. If the target is a goblinoid, it subtracts 2d4 instead of 1d4.
Once you use this property, you can't do so again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

description.name: Destroying the Horn
description.value: It's said that only the fire of Jharaashta, the dragon who sacrificed his horn for its creation, can destroy the horn. But after nine thousand years, most sages assume that the mighty dragon is long dead.
(Requires the __Mark of Hospitality__)
This ceramic jug appears to be able to hold a gallon of liquid and weighs 12 pounds whether full or empty. The jug sloshes when it is shaken, even if the jug is empty.

You can take a Magic action and name one liquid from the Alchemy Jug Liquids table to cause the jug to produce the chosen liquid. Afterward, you can uncork the jug as a Utilize action and pour that liquid out, up to 2 gallons per minute. The maximum amount of liquid the jug can produce depends on the liquid you named.
Once the jug starts producing a liquid, it can't produce a different one, or more of one that has reached its maximum, until the next dawn.

name: Ghallanda Cauldron
type: common (requires attunement by a Creature with the __Mark of Hospitality__)

description.value: Engraved with arcane sigils and imbued with ground Siberys shards, this cauldron allows you to prepare food in the blink of an eye. While you have to provide the raw materials, a Ghallanda Cauldron can mystically heat, chill, or flavor contents, allowing precise control over temperature and replicating the flavor of spices or herbs you don't possess. While cooking food in the cauldron, you can reduce its cooking time by 90%, and you gain Advantage on ability checks made using Cook's Utensils.

This bow is hand-carved carefully from the bones of a dryad and stained in the undead blood of vampires. Strung with the hair of a banshee with a powerful wraith animus is placed within the handle. Once the bow's crafting is complete, it fades from its physical form into a semi-corporeal form.
You gain a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic longbow.
The bow produces its own spectral ammunition which deals Force damage instead of Piercing damage. The ammunition disappears when it hits or misses a target.

While attuned to this weapon, you can use a Bonus Action to see into the Ethereal Plane and see all invisible creatures and objects until the end of your turn. Additionally, you can see through all walls and solid objects within 60 feet of you until the end of your turn. During this time, ammunition fired from this bow passes through solid objects, and you can target enemies within 60 feet of you with your ranged attacks, even if they are behind total cover. You can use this Bonus Action only if you haven't moved during your turn. After you use the Bonus Action, your Speed becomes 0 until the end of your turn.

description.name: Crafting
description.value: Creating a Ghost Sight Bow requires a Very Rare Workshop and the following Very Rare Components:

entries: **[Animus]**: Undead Animus from a Wraith
**[Bones]**: Skull from a Dryad
**[Dust]**: Undead Dust
**[Fluid]**: Ectoplasm
**[Fluid]**: Monster Blood from an Undead
**[Hair]**: Hair from a Banshee

This club is made from the cleaned and polished femur of a giant, crafted finely into a usable two-handed club. Its tapered hilt is wrapped in stained leather. Fastened to the top of the club is a large troll skull with several monstrous teeth embedded into it like a bone morningstar, giving the weapon a grim appearance. The club is imbued with elemental power from the animus used to power the weapon, which causes it to crackle with elemental power.
You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic greatclub, and you have Advantage on attack rolls made against Giants.
While attuned to this club you deal an additional **2d6** damage of the type associated with the elemental dust infused into it.

description.name: Crafting
description.value: Creating a Giant Femur Club requires a Rare Workshop and the following Rare Components:

entries: **[Animus]**: Giant Animus from a Troll
**[Bone]**: Skull from a Troll
**[Bone]**: Bone from a Giant
**[Dust]**: Elemental Dust from a Troll
**[Hide]**: Skin from a Monstrosity
**[Natural Weapons]**: Teeth from a Giant, Beast, or Monstrosity

description.value: The dust component determines the additional damage the club deals. For example, dust from a __Storm Troll__ deals Lightning damage, and dust from an __Eldritch Troll__ causes the club to deal Necrotic damage.

description.name: Two-Handed
description.value: A Two-Handed weapon requires two hands when you attack with it.

description.name: Push
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can push the creature up to 10 feet straight away from yourself if it is Large or smaller.

description.name: Thrown
description.value: If a weapon has the Thrown property, you can throw the weapon to make a ranged attack, and you can draw that weapon as part of the attack. If the weapon is a Melee weapon, use the same ability modifier for the attack and damage rolls that you use for a melee attack with that weapon.

description.name: Entangling
description.value: When you take the Attack action on your turn and hit with an Entangling weapon, you can use a Bonus Action later on the same turn to entangle the target. The target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw (DC 10 plus your Proficiency Bonus) or have the Grappled condition until it escapes or until you release the weapon. The target succeeds automatically if it is Huge or larger.

To escape, the target must use an action to make a Strength (*Athletics*) or Dexterity (*Acrobatics*) check against the same DC. On a success, the target no longer has the Grappled condition. While a creature is Grappled by this weapon, you can't use it to attack a different creature.

While wearing this armor, you have Resistance to Radiant damage. Whenever a creature hits or misses you with a melee attack, it takes **3** Piercing damage. An attacker can choose to have Disadvantage on its attack roll to avoid this damage.
Your Dexterity score is 19 while you wear these ratling hide gloves. They have no effect on you if your Dexterity is 19 or higher without them.

description.name: Crafting
description.value: Creating Gloves of Ratling Agility requires a Rare Workshop and the following Rare Components:

entries: **[Animus]**: Any Animus
**[Hair]**: Fur from any Ratling
**[Hide]**: Skin from any Ratling
**[Organ]**: Guts from any Monstrosity

description.value: These gloves come in pairs, each one tied to a small pocket dimension. The gloves' weight is negligible, regardless of their contents. While wearing the gloves, and holding an object that weighs no more than 20 pounds and can be held in one hand, you can take a Bonus Action to store that object inside the glove's extradimensional space. When an object is stored inside the extradimensional space, you can take a Bonus Action to summon it back into your empty hand. You can only store a single object in each glove's extradimensional space, for a total of two items between the pair.
If a glove is pierced or torn, it is destroyed, and its contents are scattered in the Astral Plane.

Placing the gloves inside an extradimensional space created by a Bag of Holding, Portable Hole, or similar item instantly destroys both items and opens a gate to the Astral Plane. The gate originates where the one item was placed inside the other. Any creature within 10 feet of the gate and not behind Total Cover is sucked through it to a random location on the Astral Plane. The gate then closes. The gate is one-way only and can't be reopened.

The ring, made from the bristles of the gold mane boar, sheds Bright Light in a 20-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 20 feet. This light shines even in areas where magic does not function, or where magical light would normally be suppressed.
These five ornate, golden rings once belonged to an evil monarch. Alone, each is simply an inert piece of dress jewellery. When they are brought together, they hum with dark and ominous energy.

The Gold Rings of Might have 5 charges, and regain 1 expended charge every day at dawn. If you expend the last charge, the item loses its enchantment and does not recharge. If a creature is wearing the Gold Rings of Might, they can innately cast the __Shocking Grasp__ spell as a Magic action.
The wearer can expend 1 charge to cast __Lightning Bolt__ (save DC 15) as a Magic action, without using the materials or a spell slot.
Alternatively, the wearer can expend 3 charges to cast __Chain Lightning__ (save DC 15) as a Magic action, without using the materials or a spell slot.
Whether this smooth, pearlescent egg was truly laid by a mythical golden goose is the subject of much debate. What is known for sure, however, is that the egg has remarkable healing powers.

Once per day as an Action, this item can be thrown into an unoccupied space up to 40 ft away and release a wave of healing energy. Creatures within a 30 ft radius Sphere from the point the Goose Egg Healing Grenade lands regain 2d8 + 4 Hit Points, or 5d8 + 4 if they are within a 10 ft radius Sphere. The item's magic heals up to six creatures at a time, starting with the creatures with the lowest Hit Points.
This item's magic has no effect on undead creatures or constructs.
A Grappling Gun can shoot a Grappling Hook attached to a rope up to 150 feet, and the hook catches with a successful DC 10 Dexterity (*Acrobatics*) check.

Additionally, if you are falling, you can use a Reaction to shoot the Grappling Gun at an attachable surface to stop your fall. You still must succeed on the check to ensure the Grappling Hook catches on a solid object. On a successful check, you stop your fall.
When you consume this potion, you immediately gain the benefits of a Long Rest.
Once you consume a Greater Rejuvenation Potion, you can't benefit from consuming another until you finish 3d6 Long Rests.

description.name: Crafting
description.value: Creating a Greater Rejuvenation Potion requires a Legendary Workshop and the following Legendary Components:

entries: **[Animus]**: Any Animus
**[Bones]**: Any Giant
**[Dust]**: Fey Dust
**[Fluid]**: Any Elemental Fluid
**[Fluid]**: Monster Blood from any Dragon
**[Hair]**: Any Celestial
**[Organ]**: Brain from an Aberration
**[Organ]**: Heart from a Fiend

name: Green Ribbon

description.value: This green satin ribbon is just long enough to fasten around a person's neck comfortably. It's hard to think why you'd even want to remove it. While you wear the ribbon, you have a +5 bonus to Death Saving Throws, and it grants the following properties.

description.name: Instant Attunement
description.value: If the ribbon is wrapped around the neck of a dead creature that has been dead no longer than 10 days and wasn't Undead when it died, the creature returns to life as if by a __Raise Dead__ spell, and it instantly attunes to the ribbon. The creature dies immediately if its Attunement to the ribbon ends or if the ribbon is removed.

description.name: Ribbon's Mending
description.value: When you drop to 0 Hit Points, you can take a Reaction to immediately regain Hit Points equal to half your level (minimum 1). Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dusk or until you roll a 20 on the d20 for a Death Saving Throw.

description.name: Curse of the Ribbon
description.value: Creatures other than you within 60 feet of you have a -1 penalty to Death Saving Throws. This penalty increases by 1 each time you use the Ribbon's Mending property.

description.name: Lingering Curses
description.value: Ending your Attunement to one of these items removes its curse, but the power of a Cursed Curio doesn't release its hold on the user easily. If you attune to it again within 28 days, the progression of its curse returns to where it was before you ended your Attunement.

properties: ending your attunement to one of these items removes its curse, but the power of a cursed curio doesn't release its hold on the user easily. if you attune to it again within 28 days, the progression of its curse returns to where it was before you ended your attunement.

description.value: This substance, harvested from the tears of a remorseful storm, proves toxic to creatures of unnatural origins. You can take an action to hurl the grenade at a point up to 30 feet away. When it lands, the grenade explodes in a 20-foot-radius Sphere. Each Aberration, Fiend, and Undead creature within the area makes a DC 17 Constitution saving throw, taking **8d6** Psychic damage on a failed save or half that much on a successful one.

A Grieving Tree is a giant skeletal tree made of the purest white marble, weighing thousands of pounds. One of the greatest inventions of the daashor Taruuzh, a Grieving Tree is part execution device and part torture device; a nearly inescapable prison that sustains victims on the very edge of death. The secrets to the tree's construction were lost with Taruuzh's death, as was the art of controlling them. To attune to a Grieving Tree, a character will have to rediscover these forgotten techniques.

description.name: Lingering Life
description.value: The tree has a pool of Hit Points. The pool starts at 20 Hit Points, and gains Hit Points whenever the tree uses its Eviscerate ability, to a maximum of 200 Hit Points. As long as there are Hit Points in this pool, whenever an imprisoned creature drops to 0 Hit Points but is still alive, that creature is healed 1d4 + 1 Hit Points and the same amount is subtracted from the pool.

description.name: Prisoners of the Tree
description.value: The tree can hold up to four creatures (or their corpses) at a time. A creature that is within 5 feet of a prisoner can attempt to free it from the tree by making a DC 20 Strength (*Athletics*) check. On a success, the prisoner is freed, and both creatures take **3d6** Piercing damage. On a failure, the prisoner remains in the tree, and both creatures take the Piercing damage.

description.name: Tree Control
description.value: While attuned to the tree and within 120 feet of it, you gain the following benefits:

entries: **Grab**: You can take a Magic action to target a creature within 20 feet of the tree. The target must make a DC 24 Dexterity saving throw as the tree reaches down to snare them. On a failed save, the tree captures the target within its branches. The target takes **6d6** Piercing damage, and has the Stunned condition until it's released from the tree.

**Eviscerate**: You can take a Magic action to command the tree to eviscerate its unfortunate prisoners, draining their life and blood as the branches shake and quiver. All creatures Stunned by the tree take **8d6** Piercing damage, and half of the total damage dealt is added to the tree's Lingering Life pool.

**Answer for Their Crimes**: You can take a Magic action to cast __Speak with Dead__ on the corpse of a creature imprisoned in the tree, without expending a spell slot or requiring Material components. When you cast the spell in this manner, the corpse is compelled to speak truthfully.
**Release a Prisoner**: You can take a Bonus Action to command the tree to release one of its prisoners.

description.value: This gruesome mixture is made from ground mouruge bones, along with rotten meat and mud. When consumed, your Strength score becomes 19 for 1 hour (unless it is already 19 or higher). You also have Disadvantage on Intelligence ability checks and saving throws for the duration.

name: Guardian Poleaxe

description.name: Damage
description.value: A Damage property weapon can deal different types of damage. When you hit with an attack from this weapon, choose one of the damage types allowed.

description.name: Hafted
description.value: A Hafted weapon's haft can function well as an off-hand attack. After you use the Attack action to attack with a Hafted weapon, you can use a Bonus Action to make a melee attack with the haft. The haft deals **1d6** Bludgeoning damage, and you add your ability modifier to damage.

description.name: Heavy
description.value: You have Disadvantage on attack rolls with a Heavy weapon if it's a Melee weapon and your Strength score isn't at least 13 or if it's a Ranged weapon and your Dexterity score isn't at least 13.

description.name: Reach
description.value: A Reach weapon adds 5 feet to your reach when you attack with it, as well as when determining your reach for Opportunity Attacks with it.

description.name: Two-Handed
description.value: A Two-Handed weapon requires two hands when you attack with it.

description.name: Set
description.value: Weapons with the Set property allow you to prepare for an oncoming attack. If a target enters your reach while you wield a weapon with this property, you can use your Reaction to make a melee attack with the weapon against that target.

properties: a hafted weapon's haft can function well as an off-hand attack. after you use the attack action to attack with a hafted weapon, you can use a bonus action to make a melee attack with the haft. the haft deals **1d6** bludgeoning damage, and you add your ability modifier to damage.

description.value: When you drink from this glass jug, you become insubstantial for 1 minute. During this time, you can move through creatures and objects as if they were Difficult Terrain, taking **1d10** Force damage if you end your turn inside an object.
The potion is stored in jugs labeled "XxX," with a skeletal smile drawn on it. The ghastly, blue-green liquor within has an overpowering smell and harsh taste.

description.name: Heightened Potency
description.value: For the duration, you gain a Fly Speed equal to your Speed.

description.name: Finesse
description.value: When making an attack with a Finesse weapon, use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

description.name: Light
description.value: When you take the Attack action on your turn and attack with a Light weapon, you can make one extra attack as a Bonus Action later on the same turn. That extra attack must be made with a different Light weapon, and you don't add your ability modifier to the extra attack's damage unless that modifier is negative. For example, you can attack with a Shortsword in one hand and a Dagger in the other using the Attack action and a Bonus Action, but you don't add your Strength or Dexterity modifier to the damage roll of the Bonus Action unless that modifier is negative.

description.name: Vex
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon and deal damage to the creature, you have Advantage on your next attack roll against that creature before the end of your next turn.

name: Handgun

description.value: Portable, reliable, and with a generous magazine size, the Handgun is the go-to firearm for self-defense and law enforcement.

description.name: Range
description.value: A Range weapon has a range in parentheses after the Ammunition or Thrown property. The range lists two numbers. The first is the weapon's normal range in feet, and the second is the weapon's long range. When attacking a target beyond normal range, you have Disadvantage on the attack roll. You can't attack a target beyond the long range.

description.name: Ammunition
description.value: You can use a weapon that has the Ammunition property to make a ranged attack only if you have ammunition to fire from it. The type of ammunition required is specified with the weapon's range. Each attack expends one piece of ammunition. Drawing the ammunition is part of the attack (you need a free hand to load a one-handed weapon). After a fight, you can spend 1 minute to recover half the ammunition (round down) you used in the fight; the rest is lost.

description.name: Firearm
description.value: You don't add your ability modifier to the weapon's damage, unless otherwise stated. Firearm ammunition is destroyed upon use.

description.name: Light
description.value: When you take the Attack action on your turn and attack with a Light weapon, you can make one extra attack as a Bonus Action later on the same turn. That extra attack must be made with a different Light weapon, and you don't add your ability modifier to the extra attack's damage unless that modifier is negative. For example, you can attack with a Shortsword in one hand and a Dagger in the other using the Attack action and a Bonus Action, but you don't add your Strength or Dexterity modifier to the damage roll of the Bonus Action unless that modifier is negative.

description.name: Reload
description.value: You can make a limited number of shots with a Reload weapon. You must then reload the weapon as an action or a Bonus Action.

description.name: Vex
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon and deal damage to the creature, you have Advantage on your next attack roll against that creature before the end of your next turn.

properties: you don't add your ability modifier to the weapon's damage, unless otherwise stated. firearm ammunition is destroyed upon use.

name: Handling Channeling Wand
type: rare (requires attunement by a Creature with the __Mark of Handling__)

description.value: This short metal wand is tipped with a Siberys dragonshard.

A Channeling Wand has 7 charges. While holding it, you can cast any spell on your __Mark of Handling__ list, expending a number of charges equal to the level of the spell you cast. Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the other spells you can cast using your Dragonmark feat. You can expend additional charges to enhance the spell, choosing one of the following effects:

entries: **Casting Time**: You expend 2 charges to change a spell that normally has a casting time of 1 Magic action to instead be cast as a Bonus Action.
**Duration**: You expend 1 charge to double the duration of the spell, to a maximum of 24 hours.
**Range**: You expend 1 charge to double the range of the spell. If the spell normally has a range of Touch, you can cast it with a range of 30 feet.
**Regaining Charges**: The wand regains 1d6 + 1 expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the wand's last charge, roll 1d20. On a 1, the wand crumbles into ashes and is destroyed.

name: Handling Dragonmark Channel
type: common (requires attunement by a Creature with the __Mark of Handling__)

description.value: This brooch is embedded with a small Siberys dragonshard, usually depicting the crest of its dragonmarked house.
While wearing a Dragonmark Channel, you can use it to cast any level 1 spell on your __Mark of Handling__ list. Once you use the channel, it can't be used again until you finish a Long Rest.
Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the spells you can cast with your Dragonmark feat.

name: Handling Dragonmark Reservoir
type: uncommon (requires attunement by a Creature with the __Mark of Handling__)

description.value: Dragonmark Reservoirs are always embedded with a Siberys dragonshard, but come in many forms, most commonly an amulet or bracelet bearing the design of the house crest.

A Dragonmark Reservoir has 7 charges. While wearing it, you can use it to cast any spell on your __Mark of Handling__ list at 1st or 2nd level, expending a number of charges equal to the level of the spell you cast. The reservoir regains 1d6 + 1 expended charges daily at dawn. Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the spells you can cast with your Dragonmark feat.

When you drink this potion, you are filled with good health and bounty, providing you with enough nourishment to sustain you for 1 day. For the next hour, when you regain Hit Points, you regain additional Hit Points equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
The potion's bottle is made from a hollowed-out gourd, and the thick, liquid inside is a deep orange that tastes of nutmeg and cardamom.

description.name: Heightened Potency
description.value: The additional Hit Points you regain are equal to half your level rather than your Proficiency Bonus (minimum +2).

This crimson and gold hooded cape is fitted with the feathers of fallen Harpies and dyed in their blood, this grants the wearer some resistance to the songs of Harpies. The cape is then infused with the dust of a fey creature which grants it a powerful anti-charm effect powered by an animus.
While wearing this cape, you have Advantage on saving throws against the Charmed and Frightened conditions.

description.name: Crafting
description.value: Creating a Hazewind Cape requires an Uncommon Workshop and the following Uncommon Components:

entries: **[Animus]**: Animus from a Harpy
**[Dust]**: Fey Dust
**[Fluid]**: Monster Blood from a Harpy
**[Hair]**: Feathers from a Harpy
**[Hide]**: Skin

name: Healing Channeling Wand
type: rare (requires attunement by a Creature with the __Mark of Healing__)

description.value: This short metal wand is tipped with a Siberys dragonshard.

A Channeling Wand has 7 charges. While holding it, you can cast any spell on your __Mark of Healing__ list, expending a number of charges equal to the level of the spell you cast. Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the other spells you can cast using your Dragonmark feat. You can expend additional charges to enhance the spell, choosing one of the following effects:

entries: **Casting Time**: You expend 2 charges to change a spell that normally has a casting time of 1 Magic action to instead be cast as a Bonus Action.
**Duration**: You expend 1 charge to double the duration of the spell, to a maximum of 24 hours.
**Range**: You expend 1 charge to double the range of the spell. If the spell normally has a range of Touch, you can cast it with a range of 30 feet.
**Regaining Charges**: The wand regains 1d6 + 1 expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the wand's last charge, roll 1d20. On a 1, the wand crumbles into ashes and is destroyed.

name: Healing Dragonmark Channel
type: common (requires attunement by a Creature with the __Mark of Healing__)

description.value: This brooch is embedded with a small Siberys dragonshard, usually depicting the crest of its dragonmarked house.
While wearing a Dragonmark Channel, you can use it to cast any level 1 spell on your __Mark of Healing__ list. Once you use the channel, it can't be used again until you finish a Long Rest.
Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the spells you can cast with your Dragonmark feat.

name: Healing Dragonmark Reservoir
type: uncommon (requires attunement by a Creature with the __Mark of Healing__)

description.value: Dragonmark Reservoirs are always embedded with a Siberys dragonshard, but come in many forms, most commonly an amulet or bracelet bearing the design of the house crest.

A Dragonmark Reservoir has 7 charges. While wearing it, you can use it to cast any spell on your __Mark of Healing__ list at 1st or 2nd level, expending a number of charges equal to the level of the spell you cast. The reservoir regains 1d6 + 1 expended charges daily at dawn. Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the spells you can cast with your Dragonmark feat.

The Hearthfire Breastplate has been profoundly transformed by its corruption. Once it was emblazoned with a golden sun and radiated light. Now its surface is black and distorted, wriggling as if the metal were alive.

description.name: Aspirant
description.value: At this tier of Attunement, you have the following benefits while wearing the Hearthfire Breastplate:

entries: You can cast the __Shield__ spell a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus. You regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.
You gain a +2 bonus to Armor Class and saving throws.

description.value: You also gain the following curse:

entries: Though the breastplate isn't heavy, it feels burdensome, even when you aren't wearing it. You have Disadvantage on Dexterity saving throws.

description.name: Adept
description.value: At the Adept tier of Attunement, you have the following additional benefits while wearing the Hearthfire Breastplate:

entries: Take a Magic action to choose up to six creatures you can see within 30 feet of you. Each creature gains 1d4 + 5 Temporary Hit Points. You can use this property a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, regaining all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.
Creatures other than you have a +2 bonus to Armor Class while they have Temporary Hit Points provided by the breastplate.

description.value: You also gain the following curse:

entries: You feel the pain of the companions you try to protect. When an ally within 60 feet takes damage that reduces their Temporary Hit Points, you take Psychic damage equal to half the number of Temporary Hit Points lost. This damage can't be reduced or avoided in any way.

description.name: Master
description.value: While at the Master tier of Attunement, you have the following additional benefit while wearing the Hearthfire Breastplate:

entries: When a creature you can see within 30 feet of you takes damage, you can take a Reaction to ward that creature. It has Immunity to all damage until the start of your next turn, including against the triggering damage. You can use this property once, regaining the ability to do so after you finish a Long Rest.

description.value: You also gain the following curse:

entries: Seeing your companions fall fills you with dreadful guilt. When an ally that you can see drops to 0 Hit Points, you have the Frightened condition for 1 minute. If the creature dies, you have the Paralyzed condition instead. At the end of each of your turns, you can make a DC 16 Wisdom saving throw, ending the condition on a success.

description.value: This golden trumpet is never dulled by rust or dirt. As an action, you can blow the trumpet to create a rousing battle call that can be heard up to **600 feet** away.

When you use the trumpet, choose up to 12 willing creatures within **600 feet** to become emboldened. An emboldened creature has Immunity to the Frightened condition and Advantage on Wisdom saving throws. In addition, its Hit Point maximum increases by 2d10 and it regains the same number of Hit Points. These benefits last for 8 hours.
If you are a Fiend or Undead creature, you take **8d6** Radiant damage when you blow the trumpet.
Once you use Heaven's Herald, it cannot be used again until the next dawn.

This helm is forged in fires ignited with elemental dust, using plates from a construct and the heart of a red dragon. The plates are then soaked in elemental fluid before having an animus gem installed that contains the energy of a Fire Giant.

While your Rage is active, you gain Resistance to Fire damage. In addition, once per turn, while you are Raging, when you hit a target with a Melee weapon that benefitted from your Reckless Attack feature, the target becomes Burning (2d4 Fire).

description.name: Crafting
description.value: Creating a Helm of Burning Rage requires a Rare Workshop and the following Rare Components:

entries: **[Animus]**: Animus from a Fire Giant
**[Dust]**: Elemental Dust
**[Fluid]**: Elemental Fluid
**[Hide]**: Plates
**[Organ]**: Heart from a Red Dragon

name: Helm of the Sentinel
type: rare (requires attunement by a Creature with the __Mark of Sentinel__)

description.value: This helm has 3 charges. While wearing it, you can use any of its properties. It regains all expended charges daily at dawn.

description.name: Counterspell
description.value: You can take a Magic action to expend 1 charge and establish a defensive ward with a contingent __Counterspell__. The next time you can see an unfriendly creature within 60 feet of you casting any spell that either targets you or causes you to make a saving throw, the __Counterspell__ immediately takes effect whether or not you want it to, as if you had cast it using your Reaction. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for this spell. The ward ends immediately after __Counterspell__ takes effect or at the next dawn.

description.name: Protection
description.value: You can take a Magic action to expend 1 charge and cast __Protection from Energy__ on yourself.

description.name: Deflection Field
description.value: You can take a Bonus Action to expend 1 charge and cast __Shield of Faith__ on yourself.

name: Hide of the Brimstone Behemoth (Legendary)

description.value: This cloak was made from the hide of a reptilian magma Fiend, incomparable in its destructive power. Flame now shies away from it, for one who has mastered such a titanic creature can master its element.
While wearing this cloak, you gain a +3 bonus to Armor Class and Constitution saving throws determined by the cloak's rarity, and you can use the following properties.

description.name: Deep-Dweller (Rare+)
description.value: You have Resistance to Fire damage and a Burrow Speed equal to your Speed. Once during your turn when you emerge from burrowing, each creature in a 10-foot Emanation originating from you must make a Dexterity saving throw (DC = 16 + the hide's bonus), taking **2d8** Fire damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

description.name: Infernal Roar (Rare+)
description.value: You can cast __Fear__ (save DC = 16 + the hide's bonus) from the cloak. This property can be used three times, regaining all expended uses daily at dusk.

description.name: Hellfire Maw (Very Rare+)
description.value: As a Magic action, you can exhale hellfire in a 30-foot Cone. Each creature in the area must make a Dexterity saving throw (DC = 16 + the hide's bonus). On a failed save, a creature takes **4d6** Fire damage and **4d6** Necrotic damage, and it can't regain Hit Points for 1 minute. On a successful save, it takes half damage only. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dusk.

description.name: Pernicious Fire Immunity (Legendary)
description.value: Fire actively avoids you. You have Immunity to Fire damage. When you are the target of an attack that deals Fire damage, the attack randomly targets another creature within the attack's range, which can include the attacker. When you make a saving throw against an effect that deals Fire damage, you must choose one other creature that is also making the saving throw against that effect. It has Disadvantage on the save.

description.name: Fabled Heirloom
description.value: Each Fabled Heirloom is a magic item that grows in strength as its attuned owner gains power. The rarity of each heirloom increases as the character grows in level, as shown on the Heirloom Rarity table. An heirloom's description details the properties it always has, as well as the properties it gains as it increases in rarity. The heirloom has all the properties of its rarity and lower.

description.value: This cloak was made from the hide of a reptilian magma Fiend, incomparable in its destructive power. Flame now shies away from it, for one who has mastered such a titanic creature can master its element.
While wearing this cloak, you gain a +2 bonus to Armor Class and Constitution saving throws determined by the cloak's rarity, and you can use the following properties.

description.name: Deep-Dweller (Rare+)
description.value: You have Resistance to Fire damage and a Burrow Speed equal to your Speed. Once during your turn when you emerge from burrowing, each creature in a 10-foot Emanation originating from you must make a Dexterity saving throw (DC = 16 + the hide's bonus), taking **2d8** Fire damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

description.name: Infernal Roar (Rare+)
description.value: You can cast __Fear__ (save DC = 16 + the hide's bonus) from the cloak. This property can be used three times, regaining all expended uses daily at dusk.

description.name: Hellfire Maw (Very Rare+)
description.value: As a Magic action, you can exhale hellfire in a 30-foot Cone. Each creature in the area must make a Dexterity saving throw (DC = 16 + the hide's bonus). On a failed save, a creature takes **4d6** Fire damage and **4d6** Necrotic damage, and it can't regain Hit Points for 1 minute. On a successful save, it takes half damage only. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dusk.

description.name: Fabled Heirloom
description.value: Each Fabled Heirloom is a magic item that grows in strength as its attuned owner gains power. The rarity of each heirloom increases as the character grows in level, as shown on the Heirloom Rarity table. An heirloom's description details the properties it always has, as well as the properties it gains as it increases in rarity. The heirloom has all the properties of its rarity and lower.

description.value: This foul-tasting tea is brewed from the powdered tusks of doom boars. When you drink this potion, you gain the effect of a __Remove Curse__ spell.
Hogs' Wash can also be used as a component in removing a Shadowsteel curse (see "Shadowsteel Curses").

name: Hook of the Tall Man (Legendary)

description.value: This hook is made from a single huge claw attached to a large bleached fingerbone mounted on a haft of ash. The tip of the claw gives off an eerie glow. The finger and claw were cut from the hand of the Tall Man.
You gain a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon determined by the hook's rarity. While holding the hook, you can use the following properties.

description.name: Snare (Rare+)
description.value: When you hit a creature with the hook, you can activate the __Topple__ mastery property in addition to a different mastery property you're using with it.

description.name: Fey Haunt's Stride (Rare+)
description.value: You can cast __Misty Step__ from the hook, and when you do so, you have Advantage on your next Dexterity (*Stealth*) check made before the end of your next turn. This property can be used twice, regaining all expended uses when you roll Initiative.

description.name: Strike from Shadows (Very Rare+)
description.value: When you start your turn with the Invisible condition, you have Advantage on the first attack you make on your turn, even if the condition ends before you make the attack. If that attack hits, it deals an extra **2d6** Piercing damage.

description.name: Hunter's Hook (Legendary)
description.value: When you hit with an Opportunity Attack made with the hook, the target takes an extra **2d6** Psychic damage, and its Speed is 0 until the end of the turn.

description.name: Terrifying Stride (Legendary)
description.value: Immediately after you use the Fey Haunt's Stride property, you can choose a creature within 20 feet of you. It must succeed on a DC 19 Wisdom saving throw or have the Frightened condition until the end of your next turn. While Frightened in this way, the creature can't take the Disengage action.

description.name: Versatile
description.value: A Versatile weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property. The weapon deals that damage when used with two hands to make a melee attack.

The rarity of each heirloom increases as the character grows in level, as shown on the Heirloom Rarity table. An heirloom's description details the properties it always has, as well as the properties it gains as it increases in rarity. The heirloom has all the properties of its rarity and lower.

description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, that creature has Disadvantage on its next attack roll before the start of your next turn.

description.name: Topple
description.value: If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can force the creature to make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus the ability modifier used to make the attack roll and your Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, the creature has the Prone condition.

name: Hospitality Channeling Wand
type: rare (requires attunement by a Creature with the __Mark of Hospitality__)

description.value: This short metal wand is tipped with a Siberys dragonshard.

A Channeling Wand has 7 charges. While holding it, you can cast any spell on your __Mark of Hospitality__ list, expending a number of charges equal to the level of the spell you cast. Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the other spells you can cast using your Dragonmark feat. You can expend additional charges to enhance the spell, choosing one of the following effects:

entries: **Casting Time**: You expend 2 charges to change a spell that normally has a casting time of 1 Magic action to instead be cast as a Bonus Action.
**Duration**: You expend 1 charge to double the duration of the spell, to a maximum of 24 hours.
**Range**: You expend 1 charge to double the range of the spell. If the spell normally has a range of Touch, you can cast it with a range of 30 feet.
**Regaining Charges**: The wand regains 1d6 + 1 expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the wand's last charge, roll 1d20. On a 1, the wand crumbles into ashes and is destroyed.

name: Hospitality Dragonmark Channel
type: common (requires attunement by a Creature with the __Mark of Hospitality__)

description.value: This brooch is embedded with a small Siberys dragonshard, usually depicting the crest of its dragonmarked house.
While wearing a Dragonmark Channel, you can use it to cast any level 1 spell on your __Mark of Hospitality__ list. Once you use the channel, it can't be used again until you finish a Long Rest.
Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the spells you can cast with your Dragonmark feat.

name: Hospitality Dragonmark Reservoir
type: uncommon (requires attunement by a Creature with the __Mark of Hospitality__)

description.value: Dragonmark Reservoirs are always embedded with a Siberys dragonshard, but come in many forms, most commonly an amulet or bracelet bearing the design of the house crest.

A Dragonmark Reservoir has 7 charges. While wearing it, you can use it to cast any spell on your __Mark of Hospitality__ list at 1st or 2nd level, expending a number of charges equal to the level of the spell you cast. The reservoir regains 1d6 + 1 expended charges daily at dawn. Your spellcasting ability for this spell is the same as the spellcasting ability for the spells you can cast with your Dragonmark feat.
(Requires the __Mark of Warding__)

This engraved block of lead, approximately 1 cubic foot in size, holds an embedded Siberys dragonshard. The Houseward provides state-of-the-art magical security, and is typically embedded into the floor of the building it is supposed to protect. If any creature with the __Mark of Warding__ spends 10 minutes touching the Houseward, it can cast __Guards and Wards__ without requiring Material components. A 10,000 square foot area is protected by the spell. The duration of the spell is 24 days, but the effect ends early if the Houseward is used again to cast the spell, if a creature with the __Mark of Warding__ spends 10 minutes touching the Houseward to end its effects, or if a Houseward is removed from the area it is currently protecting. After being used to cast the spell, the Houseward can't do so again until the next dawn.

While wearing this frock and not wearing any armor, Opportunity Attack rolls against you have Disadvantage.
If you have reached at least Stage 2 of the Seraph Transformation, you have Advantage on saving throws to avoid revealing your true nature.

This glowing green liquid sends a creature's immune system into a hyperactive state. When you drink this potion, you have Immunity to Poison damage and to the Poisoned condition for 1 hour. While the effect lasts, you have Advantage on saving throws to avoid becoming cursed. When the potion's effect ends, you gain 1 level of Exhaustion.

name: Hunting Rifle

description.value: Designed for big game, Hunting Rifles are slow but accurate, requiring bolt action operation between every shot.

description.name: Range
description.value: A Range weapon has a range in parentheses after the Ammunition or Thrown property. The range lists two numbers. The first is the weapon's normal range in feet, and the second is the weapon's long range. When attacking a target beyond normal range, you have Disadvantage on the attack roll. You can't attack a target beyond the long range.

description.name: Ammunition
description.value: You can use a weapon that has the Ammunition property to make a ranged attack only if you have ammunition to fire from it. The type of ammunition required is specified with the weapon's range. Each attack expends one piece of ammunition. Drawing the ammunition is part of the attack (you need a free hand to load a one-handed weapon). After a fight, you can spend 1 minute to recover half the ammunition (round down) you used in the fight; the rest is lost.

description.name: Firearm
description.value: You don't add your ability modifier to the weapon's damage, unless otherwise stated. Firearm ammunition is destroyed upon use.

description.name: Reload
description.value: You can make a limited number of shots with a Reload weapon. You must then reload the weapon as an action or a Bonus Action.

description.name: Two-Handed
description.value: A Two-Handed weapon requires two hands when you attack with it.

description.name: Sighted
description.value: Attacking at long range with this weapon doesn't impose Disadvantage on your attack rolls. When you hit a creature with an attack using this weapon at long range, you can reroll any of the damage dice and must use the new roll.

properties: you don't add your ability modifier to the weapon's damage, unless otherwise stated. firearm ammunition is destroyed upon use.

name: Hypnovulfen Figure

description.value: This carved wooden figurine depicts a crooked wolf with large, leering eyes and a wild, toothy maw. While holding the figure, you can use it as a Spellcasting Focus, and you gain a +1 bonus to spell attack rolls and spell save DCs. The figure has the following properties.

description.name: Hypnovulfen Bite
description.value: Your teeth become viciously sharp. You can bite as an Unarmed Strike that deals **1d6** Piercing damage instead of Bludgeoning damage.

description.name: Hypnovulfen Eye
description.value: While holding the figure, you can cast __Confusion__ (save DC 14) with it. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dusk.

description.name: Cursed Hunger
description.value: When you roll Initiative, you must succeed on a DC 0 Wisdom saving throw or you can't use the Attack or Magic actions except to use the figure's properties until you hit a creature with a Hypnovulfen Bite attack. When you use the Hypnovulfen Eye property, the DC of this saving throw increases by 2.

description.name: Lingering Curses
description.value: Ending your Attunement to one of these items removes its curse, but the power of a Cursed Curio doesn't release its hold on the user easily. If you attune to it again within 28 days, the progression of its curse returns to where it was before you ended your Attunement.

name: Idol of the Beast of Blight (Legendary)

description.value: Made of bleached and mutated bone, this idol in the shape of a stag contains the sinister knowledge of the Beast of Blight. It pulses with the power of rot and decay.

While holding the idol, you can use it as a Spellcasting Focus for your spells, you gain a +3 bonus to spell attack rolls and your spell save DC determined by the idol's rarity, and you can use the following properties.

description.name: Rotting Touch (Rare+)
description.value: You can use your Strength, Dexterity, or Wisdom modifier for the attack and damage rolls of your Unarmed Strikes, and on a hit, your strike deals an extra **1d6** Necrotic damage (Rare), **1d8** Necrotic damage (Very Rare), or **1d10** Necrotic damage (Legendary).

description.name: Touch of Oblivion (Rare+)
description.value: As a Bonus Action, you can touch a creature that has been dead for less than 1 hour. It rots away to bleached bone and can't be used for this property again. The next time you hit with an Unarmed Strike using the Rotting Touch property before the end of your next turn, it is a Critical Hit instead.

description.name: Hallucinatory Spores (Very Rare+)
description.value: When you cast a spell using a spell slot or from the idol, you can choose one creature that you can see within 10 feet of you. It must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC = 16 + the idol's bonus) or take **2d6** Psychic damage and have Disadvantage on attack rolls until the start of your next turn.

description.name: Rot in the Flesh (Very Rare+)
description.value: You can cast __Barkskin__ from the idol targeting only yourself. For the duration, a creature that hits you with a melee attack roll takes **1d8** Necrotic damage. Once the spell is cast from the idol, it can't be cast from it again until the next dusk.

description.name: Hollow with Rot (Legendary)
description.value: When you regain Hit Points from a spell, you also gain Temporary Hit Points equal to the spell's level.

description.name: Fabled Heirloom
description.value: Each Fabled Heirloom is a magic item that grows in strength as its attuned owner gains power. The rarity of each heirloom increases as the character grows in level, as shown on the Heirloom Rarity table. An heirloom's description details the properties it always has, as well as the properties it gains as it increases in rarity. The heirloom has all the properties of its rarity and lower.

description.value: Indorius's Crown bestows authority on whoever wears it, making their reasoning seem stronger and their coercions harder to resist. The crown does not, however, provide its wearer with wisdom.

description.name: Aspirant
description.value: At this tier of Attunement, you have the following benefits while wearing Indorius's Crown:

entries: You have Advantage on Charisma ability checks and saving throws.

The crown has 12 charges. You can expend 1 or more charges to cast one of the following spells (save DC 18) from it: __Compulsion__ (4 charges), __Dominate Person__ (5 charges), __Hellish Rebuke__ (1 charge), __Hold Person__ (2 charges), or __Suggestion__ (2 charges). The crown regains 2d4 + 4 expended charges at dawn.

description.value: You also gain the following curse:

entries: Your sense of authority means you tend to pay less attention to the needs of others. While attuned to the crown, you have Disadvantage on Wisdom (*Insight*) checks and Wisdom saving throws.

description.name: Adept
description.value: At the Adept tier of Attunement, you have the following additional benefits while wearing Indorius's Crown:

entries: You can take a Bonus Action to choose a Friendly creature who can see or hear you. That creature must immediately use its Reaction to make a Weapon Attack or Unarmed Strike, or to cast a cantrip or spell of level 2 or lower with a casting time of Action. You can use this property a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, regaining all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.
Friendly creatures within 10 feet of you who can see or hear you add 1d4 to attack rolls and saving throws. You do not grant this benefit while you have the Unconscious condition.

description.value: You also gain the following curse:

entries: Your judgmental stare intimidates your companions. When an ally within 10 feet of you misses with an attack roll or fails an ability check, they have the Frightened condition from you until the end of their next turn, even if they have Immunity to the Frightened condition.

That creature must immediately use its Reaction to make a Weapon Attack or Unarmed Strike, or to cast a cantrip or spell of level 2 or lower with a casting time of Action. You can use this property a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, regaining all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.
Friendly creatures within 10 feet of you who can see or hear you add 1d4 to attack rolls and saving throws. You do not grant this benefit while you have the Unconscious condition.

description.value: You also gain the following curse:

entries: Your judgmental stare intimidates your companions. When an ally within 10 feet of you misses with an attack roll or fails an ability check, they have the Frightened condition from you until the end of their next turn, even if they have Immunity to the Frightened condition.

description.name: Master
description.value: While at the Master tier of Attunement, you have the following additional benefits while wearing Indorius's Crown:

entries: After you make a Charisma check, you can replace the number you roll with a 14.

You can cast the following spells (save DC 18) from the crown: __Dominate Monster__ and __Power Word Stun__. Once you have cast one of these spells from the crown, you can't cast either spell from the crown until you finish a Long Rest.

description.value: You also gain the following curse:

entries: You feel a sickening terror and Vulnerability when you're alone. If you can't see or hear any Friendly creatures within 10 feet of you, you have Disadvantage on attack rolls and can't concentrate on spells. Creatures conjured or summoned by magic, such as the __Find Familiar__ spell, don't count for this effect.

description.value: Designed to aid in the capture and interrogation of mages, this silver syrup is also an effective method of freeing oneself from a cursed item. After drinking this potion, you are incapable of attuning to magic items for 1 hour. During this duration, you can take an action to sever all your Attunements to magic items (even cursed items). At the end of this duration, if you are attuned to any magic items, you die.
(Requires Use by a Warforged)

This item attaches to the body of a warforged, and is designed to serve as one of the following tools that weighs 10 pounds or less: an Artisan's Tools, Forgery Kit, Herbalism Kit, Poisoner's Kit, Thieves' Tools, or a Musical Instrument.

You must incorporate the tool into your body before you can use it. Over the course of 1 hour, you can attach the tool or remove it from your body, remaining in contact with it for the whole hour; this can be done over a Short or Long Rest.

While you're alive, the tool can't be removed from your body against your will. Though the tool has become part of your body, you must still have a hand free to make use of it. You can only have one Integrated Tool attached to your body at a time.

*Eberron: Rising from the Last War introduces the Prosthetic Limb, a Common magic item requiring Attunement which predates the warforged. Prosthetic Limbs come in many forms; one might resemble an organic limb of animated wood, and another could be a metal shell or a construct of force. During the Last War, Karrnath made use of skeletal prosthetics, and more recently, Cannith and Jorasco have produced prosthetics that use the same semiorganic materials as the warforged.*
*Eberron: Rising from the Last War also includes two magic items designed to integrate into a Warforged's forearm: the Armblade and the Wand Sheath. At the DM's discretion, a character of a different species might be able to integrate one of these warforged items into their Prosthetic Limb; the question is if the two can logically work together, or if the style of your prosthetic makes it implausible that it could mesh with a warforged component. If the DM decides it's possible to integrate a component item with the prosthetic, the two could be counted as a single magic item for the purpose of determining the number of magic items you can attune to. If you remove the component from the prosthetic, you immediately lose your Attunement to the component.*
This shimmering breastplate is forged from a giant dragonfly's carapace and adorned with a cape of gossamer fabric. You gain a +1 bonus to Armor Class while you wear this armor.
While wearing this armor, you can take an action to transform the cape into dragonfly wings for 1 hour. While this effect lasts, you have a Fly Speed of 30 feet.
If you have reached at least Stage 1 of the Fey Transformation, the armor's effect lasts for 2 hours, during which time you have a Fly Speed of 60 feet.
Once this effect is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

These iron tooth caps are inscribed with magical runes. You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls with your Bite attacks, and your Bite attacks deal your choice of either force or Piercing damage.
This net is comprised of tiny interlocking iron rings. It acts as a normal Net, with the following changes:

entries: The Iron Net's range is 10 feet.
The DC of the Strength (*Athletics*) check to escape is 15.
The Iron Net has AC 13 and 15 HP.

name: Jinxed Poker Chip

description.value: This ceramic poker chip is painted with a crocodile's skull on one side. Hoarse laughter sounds when it flips. While you hold the chip, it grants the following properties.

description.name: Jinxed Luck
description.value: When you fail a D20 Test, you can take a Reaction to flip the chip. Roll 1d6. On a 4-6, you succeed on the D20 Test instead. After you use this property, roll 1d20. On a 1-5, this property can't be used again until the next dusk.

description.name: Sense Cheating
description.value: If you have proficiency with a Gaming Set, you automatically succeed on ability checks to know if someone in a game you are playing is cheating.

description.name: Cursed Coin
description.value: When you roll Initiative, you must succeed on a DC 0 Charisma saving throw or become cursed until you finish a Short or Long Rest. While cursed, you subtract 1d6 from D20 Tests. When you use the Jinxed Luck property, the saving throw DC increases by 1.

description.name: Lingering Curses
description.value: Ending your Attunement to one of these items removes its curse, but the power of a Cursed Curio doesn't release its hold on the user easily. If you attune to it again within 28 days, the progression of its curse returns to where it was before you ended your Attunement.

properties: ending your attunement to one of these items removes its curse, but the power of a cursed curio doesn't release its hold on the user easily. if you attune to it again within 28 days, the progression of its curse returns to where it was before you ended your attunement.

description.value: When you drink this brightly colored rum, your luck takes a strange turn for 1 hour. For the duration, when you make a D20 Test, roll 1d4. On a 2-4, add the number to your roll. On a 1, roll an extra d20 and use the lowest roll for the test.
This potion is stored in a glass rum bottle marked with crossbones.

description.name: Heightened Potency
description.value: Roll 1d6 instead of 1d4.

name: Jora Charm
type: common (requires attunement by a Creature with the __Mark of Healing__)

description.value: While wearing this pendant, you gain the following benefits.

description.name: Life Preservation
description.value: Whenever you make a Death Saving Throw, you can change a roll of 9 or lower to a 10, turning a failed save into a successful one.

description.name: Natural Healing Boost
description.value: Whenever you roll a Hit Point Die to regain Hit Points, double the number of Hit Points it restores.

These infamous weapons, prized by assassins, have a Khyber dragonshard embedded into the pommel that channels the souls of victims, but doesn't itself trap them. There's much debate over the actual fate of the souls of those slain by a Keeper's Fang. Common myth says that the souls of victims are trapped in the Lair of the Keeper, and heroes can seek to reclaim a soul from the Sovereign of Death and Decay. Another myth maintains that these weapons channel souls to the overlord Katashka, and that one must deal with the Lords of Dust to restore a victim. Most Keeper's Fangs were created by the Shaarat'khesh assassins of the Empire of Dhakaan. Rather than ascribing the blade's power to the Keeper--whose existence the Dhakaani reject--they believe these blades utterly destroy the souls of their victims.

You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. Whenever you use it to reduce a creature to 0 Hit Points, the creature is slain and its soul removed. A creature whose soul has been stolen in this way can be restored to life only by means of a __Wish__ spell.

description.name: Finesse
description.value: When making an attack with a Finesse weapon, use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. You must use the same modifier for both rolls.

description.name: Light
description.value: When you take the Attack action on your turn and attack with a Light weapon, you can make one extra attack as a Bonus Action later on the same turn. That extra attack must be made with a different Light weapon, and you don't add your ability modifier to the extra attack's damage unless that modifier is negative. For example, you can attack with a Shortsword in one hand and a Dagger in the other using the Attack action and a Bonus Action, but you don't add your Strength or Dexterity modifier to the damage roll of the Bonus Action unless that modifier is negative.

description.name: Thrown
description.value: If a weapon has the Thrown property, you can throw the weapon to make a ranged attack, and you can draw that weapon as part of the attack. If the weapon is a Melee weapon, use the same ability modifier for the attack and damage rolls that you use for a melee attack with that weapon.

description.name: Nick
description.value: When you make the extra attack of the Light property, you can make it as part of the Attack action instead of as a Bonus Action. You can make this extra attack only once per turn.
This cloak is made from the skin of twenty knifewings. While wearing it, you gain a +1 bonus to Armor Class. If you fall, you descend 60 feet per round and take no damage from falling.

description.name: Momentum
description.value: Momentum weapons allow you to deliver devastating attacks as part of rapid movement. When you hit with a Momentum weapon after you moved 20 feet or more in a straight line during the same turn, upgrade the damage dice to the weapon's Momentum Dice value.

description.name: Reach
description.value: A Reach weapon adds 5 feet to your reach when you attack with it, as well as when determining your reach for Opportunity Attacks with it.

description.name: Two-Handed
description.value: A Two-Handed weapon requires two hands when you attack with it.

description.name: Set
description.value: Weapons with the Set property allow you to prepare for an oncoming attack. If a target enters your reach while you wield a weapon with this property, you can use your Reaction to make a melee attack with the weapon against that target.

description.name: Versatile
description.value: A Versatile weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property. The weapon deals that damage when used with two hands to make a melee attack.

description.name: Defending
description.value: A Defending weapon is either made for parrying, has advanced techniques for use in parrying, or both. When wielding a Defending weapon, you may use your Reaction when you are hit by a melee attack roll. Roll 1d4 and add the result to your AC, including against the triggering attack.
(Requires the __Mark of Warding__)

You can take a Utilize action to place these shackles on a creature that has the Incapacitated condition. The shackles adjust to fit a creature of Small to Large size. The shackles prevent a creature bound by them from using any method of extradimensional movement, including teleportation or travel to a different plane of existence. They don't prevent the creature from passing through an interdimensional portal.

You and any creature you designate when you use the shackles can take a Utilize action to remove them. Once every 30 days, the bound creature can make a DC 30 Strength (*Athletics*) check. On a successful check, the creature breaks free and destroys the shackles.
While you are holding this wand, you can take a Magic action to instantaneously light or snuff out a candle, torch, small campfire, or similar source of flame within 10 feet of you.

name: Lantern of the Chained Reaper (Legendary)

description.value: This ornate Hooded Lantern was once a weapon in the hands of the Chained Reaper, filled with ghastly balefire. Able to pierce the veil, the lantern reveals a glimpse at things hidden from mortal eyes.

While you hold the lantern and it is lit, you gain a +3 bonus to Intelligence (*Investigation*) and Wisdom (*Perception*) checks determined by the lantern's rarity, and you can use the following properties.

description.name: Ghostly Flame (Rare+)
description.value: The lantern doesn't require fuel, and it sheds blue-green light. It casts Bright Light in a 30-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 30 feet. You can snuff or ignite its light as a Bonus Action while you are within 30 feet of it.

description.name: Revealing Flame (Rare+)
description.value: Creatures in the Border Ethereal within the area of the lantern's Bright Light are visible to creatures on the Material Plane. When a creature within the lantern's Bright Light is possessed or affected by the __Magic Jar__ spell, the creature in control appears overlaid on the body in a spectral form.

description.name: Mystic Sight (Very Rare+)
description.value: You can cast __Detect Magic__ from the lantern. The spell ends early if you extinguish the light or aren't holding the lantern.

description.name: Summon Spirit (Very Rare+)
description.value: As a Magic action, you can summon a __Ghost__ that appears in an unoccupied space you can see within 30 feet of you. The ghost obeys your commands, and it takes its turn immediately after you on your Initiative count. The ghost vanishes after 1 minute, or when it dies. You can't use the lantern's properties, except for Ghostly Flame, during this time.

description.name: Balefire (Legendary)
description.value: You can cast __Scorching Ray__ (level 5 version, +11 to hit) from the lantern. This property can be used three times, regaining all expended uses daily at dusk.

description.name: Warding Light (Legendary)
description.value: The lantern's area of Bright Light offers the protection of a __Magic Circle__ spell. This protection can't operate in the reverse direction, and it ends if you aren't holding the lantern or if you have the Incapacitated condition.

description.name: Fabled Heirloom
description.value: Each Fabled Heirloom is a magic item that grows in strength as its attuned owner gains power. The rarity of each heirloom increases as the character grows in level, as shown on the Heirloom Rarity table. An heirloom's description details the properties it always has, as well as the properties it gains as it increases in rarity. The heirloom has all the properties of its rarity and lower.
